title: Fynd ERP Product Cookbook
description: A visual, self-serve guide to setting up Fynd ERP, launching production, operating the shop floor, and tracing every finished unit.

sections.title: Start Here
sections.label: Start with Fynd ERP
sections.description: Learn the manufacturing basics, understand how Fynd ERP records connect, and see the complete journey before configuring anything.

pages.title: Fynd ERP in Plain Language
pages.summary: Understand what Fynd ERP does without needing a manufacturing background.

diagram.intro: Fynd ERP is the digital control layer between a production plan and the real work performed in the factory. This is the full journey of one production run.

nodes.title: Decide what to make
nodes.description: A production need becomes a Product, quantity, and due date. Nothing has started on the shop floor yet.
nodes.relation: defines the demand that must be prepared

nodes.title: Prepare the factory and product
nodes.description: Fynd ERP needs Lines, Stations, Shifts, a Product, an active BOM, and a Routing so it knows where, when, and how the Product can be built.
nodes.relation: makes the production plan executable

nodes.title: Release a Work Order
nodes.description: The Work Order authorises a specific quantity. Fynd ERP checks the setup, capacity, materials, identifiers, and finished-unit serials before release.
nodes.relation: creates one controlled unit record for every output

nodes.title: Build each unit
nodes.description: Every finished unit becomes a Production Task that moves through the Routing one Station at a time while work and material use are recorded.
nodes.relation: creates the evidence used to verify the result

nodes.title: Inspect and trace
nodes.description: Quality results, exceptions, consumed materials, containers, and shipment records form a history that can be searched for each finished-unit serial.

steps: Use Fynd ERP to turn a production plan into controlled work on real factory lines.
Give every unit a route, a production task, and a history that can be traced later.
Use checks, repair paths, packaging, and dashboards to keep production reliable.
rules: Fynd ERP manages manufacturing execution; it does not replace the physical factory.
Master data describes what can happen. Transaction data records what actually happened.
The setup sequence matters because downstream records depend on upstream records.
checklist: I can explain the difference between setup data and production activity.
I understand that a finished unit moves through a routing one station at a time.
I know that Fynd ERP keeps a traceable record for every released unit.

pages.title: Manufacturing Basics for New Users
pages.summary: Learn the small set of factory concepts used throughout the cookbook.

diagram.intro: Imagine one physical product moving from raw material to a customer. These concepts describe what happens to it.

nodes.title: Material
nodes.description: A Component is something consumed to make the Product. It may be tracked by lot, by serial number, or simply by quantity.
nodes.relation: is consumed while performing an

nodes.title: Operation
nodes.description: An Operation is a piece of work such as assembly, testing, inspection, or packaging.
nodes.relation: is performed at a physical

nodes.title: Station
nodes.description: A Station is the work point where the Operation happens. Stations are arranged into a Routing.
nodes.relation: changes the in-progress item into a

nodes.title: Finished unit
nodes.description: The output is one completed unit with its own serial number, Production Task, material history, and quality history.
nodes.relation: is packed into a container and linked to a

nodes.title: Shipment
nodes.description: The shipment record connects verified containers and finished units to dispatch, completing the traceability chain.

steps: A product is the item the factory intends to make.
A bill of materials lists the components required to make that product.
A routing lists the operations and stations the unit must pass through.
A work order authorises a quantity of that product to be produced.
A production task represents one finished unit moving through the route.
rules: A Line is a production lane; a Station is a specific place where an operation happens.
A component can be scanned by serial number or consumed by quantity.
A failed operation can send the unit to repair, rework, hold, or scrap depending on configuration.
checklist: I can distinguish a product, component, BOM, routing, work order, and production task.
I understand the difference between a Line and a Station.
I know why traceability begins before production is released.

pages.title: How Fynd ERP Data Connects
pages.summary: See the dependency chain that connects factory setup to executable production.

diagram.intro: Fynd ERP uses two setup branches—where work happens and what is being made. They meet in the Routing and Line assignment before a Work Order can run.

nodes.title: Site and Line
nodes.description: The Site identifies the physical location. The Line is the production lane that can receive and hold Production Tasks.
nodes.relation: provides the factory structure used by

nodes.title: Station and Shift
nodes.description: Stations identify the exact work points used by a Routing. Shifts identify when production is available to run.
nodes.relation: combines with the product definition

nodes.title: Product and active BOM
nodes.description: The Product identifies the finished item. Its active BOM identifies the Components and quantities required for one unit.
nodes.relation: provides the material definition required by

nodes.title: Routing and Line assignment
nodes.description: The Routing orders the work across Stations. The active Product-to-Line assignment says which Line is allowed to start that Product.
nodes.relation: makes it possible to create and schedule a

nodes.title: Work Order
nodes.description: The Work Order requests a quantity of the routed Product for a due date and Shift. It stays pending until the release checks pass.
nodes.relation: creates one unit-level record per output as

nodes.title: Production Tasks
nodes.description: Each Production Task represents one finished unit. It enters an eligible Starting Line, follows the Routing, and retains the unit's execution history.

steps: Sites locate Stations and can also group Lines.
Products use BOMs to define material requirements.
Routings connect operations to Stations and require an active BOM.
Product-to-Line assignments identify where a product can start production.
Releasing a Work Order creates unit-level Production Tasks on eligible Lines.
rules: A missing prerequisite blocks the next record even when the next screen is visible.
Projects and Product Families are recommended organisational layers, not hard execution blockers.
Production Orders are optional grouping records; Work Orders create executable production.
checklist: I can follow the dependency chain from Site to Production Task.
I know which organisational records are recommended.
I understand why a Production Order alone does not start production.

pages.title: Complete Fynd ERP Setup Journey
pages.summary: Follow the recommended order for configuring Fynd ERP and releasing the first production run.

diagram.intro: Use this as the setup map for a new Fynd ERP environment. Do not skip ahead: every required stage supplies information used by the next stage.

nodes.title: Model the factory
nodes.description: Confirm the Plant, then create Sites, Lines, operation Stations, separate Repair Stations, capacity, and Shifts.
nodes.relation: creates the locations and time windows needed to

nodes.title: Organise products
nodes.description: Create recommended Projects and Product Families, then define Components, Products, and any Variants.
nodes.relation: provides the items used to

nodes.title: Activate the material recipe
nodes.description: Review the Product's draft BOM, confirm every Component and quantity, approve it, and make one version active.
nodes.relation: allows Fynd ERP to validate and create

nodes.title: Design the production route
nodes.description: Create the Routing from Start to operation Stations to End, provide repair destinations, validate it, and activate it.
nodes.relation: defines how the Product can run after you

nodes.title: Assign eligible starting Lines
nodes.description: Assign the Product to active Lines, mark the true first production Line as a Starting Line, and set realistic capacity.
nodes.relation: makes the Product selectable when you

nodes.title: Create and release a Work Order
nodes.description: Select the Product, Routing, Shift, quantity, and due date; generate exactly one confirmed serial per output; resolve pre-start blockers; then release.
nodes.relation: creates the unit tasks used to

nodes.title: Run, inspect, package, and trace
nodes.description: Complete each Production Task through the route, record consumption and quality, handle exceptions, then package and trace the finished units.

flow: Create and release a Work Order
steps: Review the Plant and create the required Sites.
Create Lines, mark the correct initial Line as a Starting Line, and configure capacity.
Create operation Stations, dedicated Repair Stations, and Shifts.
Create recommended Projects and Product Families, followed by Components and Products.
Review the draft BOM created with the Product and activate it.
Build and activate a Routing, then assign the Product to eligible Lines.
Create a Work Order with at least one Shift, generate unit serials, validate readiness, and release.
rules: Do not create Work Orders until the Product has both a Routing and an active Line assignment.
Do not release production until the initial Line is marked as a Starting Line.
Do not bypass readiness warnings without understanding their effect on later Stations.
checklist: Every setup stage has an owner in my implementation plan.
Dependencies are complete before the first Work Order is created.
A small trial Work Order will be used before full-volume production.

pages.title: How to Use This Cookbook
pages.summary: Use the cookbook as a guided setup path, task reference, and troubleshooting tool.

diagram.intro: You can read the cookbook from beginning to end or enter through global search. Every guide uses the same five-part learning pattern.

nodes.title: Choose a journey or search
nodes.description: New users should start with the ordered navigation. Returning users can search for a record, task, error, or manufacturing term from any page.
nodes.relation: opens a guide where you first

nodes.title: Check prerequisites
nodes.description: The 'Before you begin' section lists the records or earlier knowledge that should already be complete.
nodes.relation: prevents blockers before you

nodes.title: Understand the diagram
nodes.description: The diagram explains what each record or action means and why the next step depends on it.
nodes.relation: gives context for the detailed

nodes.title: Follow the steps and rules
nodes.description: Use 'What to do' for the sequence and 'Rules to remember' for the conditions that Fynd ERP enforces.
nodes.relation: leads to the final

nodes.title: Confirm readiness
nodes.description: Complete the checklist before continuing. Required topics block the core flow; Recommended topics improve control; Conditional topics apply only when used.

steps: New users should follow the sections in the order shown in the navigation.
Experienced users can use global search from any page to find a record or task.
Use the Required, Recommended, and Conditional labels to understand priority.
Use the readiness checklist at the end of each guide before continuing.
rules: Required means Fynd ERP blocks or cannot reliably complete the downstream action without it.
Recommended means Fynd ERP may allow the action, but the setup improves organisation and control.
Conditional means the setup is needed only when that manufacturing capability is used.
checklist: I know how to search from every cookbook page.
I understand the three requirement labels.
I know where to download the complete cookbook as a PDF.

sections.title: Configure Your Factory
sections.label: Configure the Factory
sections.description: Create the physical structure Fynd ERP needs: Sites, Lines, Stations, Repair Stations, capacity, and Shifts.

pages.title: The Fynd ERP Factory Model
pages.summary: Understand how Plant, Site, Line, and Station represent a real manufacturing unit.
steps: The Plant is the overall manufacturing context used to isolate records.
A Site represents a physical location within the Plant.
A Line represents a production lane and receives Production Tasks.
A Station represents a specific operational point used in a Routing.
rules: Stations require a Site.
Lines can reference a Site, but the current Line setup does not require it.
A Station can exist without a Line assignment, although linking the physical structure is recommended.
checklist: Every operation has a clear physical Site.
Production lanes are represented as Lines.
Work areas are represented as Stations rather than additional Lines.

pages.title: Create Sites
pages.summary: Create the physical locations required before Stations can be configured.
steps: Create one Site for each physical manufacturing location that needs separate operational records.
Give each Site a unique name and code within the Plant.
Add optional address details by selecting Country before State, and State before City.
Keep optional metadata within the 32 KB limit.
Use the Site when creating Stations and, where useful, Lines and storage locations.
rules: Site name and code are the required fields; the code accepts uppercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only.
A Station cannot be created without a valid Site.
Site names and codes must be unique within the Plant.
Do not create a separate Site for every room or workstation; use Stations for that detail.
checklist: Site names and codes are unique.
Every planned Station can be mapped to a Site.
Users can distinguish Sites without relying only on codes.

pages.title: Create Production Lines
pages.summary: Create the production lanes that will receive and balance unit-level Production Tasks.
steps: Create each real production lane with a unique name and code.
Choose the Line type that best describes the manufacturing phase.
Set Capacity Per Shift above Capacity Per Hour and enter a whole-number Task Queue Capacity from 1 to 100,000.
Mark the Line that receives newly released units as a Starting Line.
Keep the Line active when it should be eligible for production.
rules: Name, code, and Line type are required; the Line code has a maximum length of 50 characters.
A Product needs at least one active Line assignment before a Work Order can be created.
Normal initial release uses only eligible Lines marked as Starting Lines.
Use a downstream phase as a Starting Line only when production can genuinely begin there.
checklist: Every production lane has a unique Line.
The initial Line is marked as a Starting Line.
Capacity reflects the number of active and waiting tasks the Line can accept.

pages.title: Create Stations and Repair Stations
pages.summary: Create operational work points and the separate repair destinations required by Routings.
steps: Create a Station for each operation that must be represented in a Routing.
Enter the required name, code, Site, and Station Category.
Use a name with at least two characters and a code containing only letters, numbers, and hyphens.
Create dedicated Repair-type Stations for failure handling.
Use a Repair Station different from the main operation Station in every Routing operation.
rules: Station name, code, Site, and Station Category are required.
Station names and codes must be unique within the Plant.
Every operation node in the current Routing builder requires a Repair Station.
The Repair Station cannot be the same Station as the operation itself.
Automatic Stations are used for configured automation; regular Stations expect operator interaction.
checklist: Every planned operation has a Station.
Every operation can point to a separate Repair Station.
Station types match the way work will be performed.

pages.title: Create Shifts
pages.summary: Define when production runs and make Shifts available for Work Order assignment.
steps: Create Shift definitions that reflect the Plant's working periods.
Enter the required name, unique code, Shift type, start time, and end time.
Use 24-hour HH:mm times; overnight Shifts are supported.
Give every break a name, type, and duration of at least one minute.
Add schedule information when production varies by day or calendar.
Select at least one valid Shift when creating each Work Order.
rules: Shift codes use uppercase letters, numbers, and hyphens.
Unpaid breaks are deducted from net working time.
A Work Order cannot be created or started without at least one Shift assignment.
Assigned Shifts must belong to the same Plant.
checklist: All active production periods are represented.
Shift times do not overlap unintentionally.
At least one Shift is ready for the first Work Order.

pages.title: Factory Readiness Checklist
pages.summary: Confirm the physical factory model is complete before creating production master data.
steps: Walk through the physical production process and match each area to a Fynd ERP record.
Confirm which Line receives the first operation for every product type.
Confirm Line capacities using a small realistic production quantity.
Confirm every operation and failure path has a usable Station.
rules: Do not compensate for missing Lines by creating extra Stations.
Do not mark every Line as a Starting Line unless units can genuinely begin there.
Repair Stations must be planned before Routings are built.
checklist: Required Sites exist.
Lines are active, correctly typed, and have explicit capacity.
Initial Lines are marked as Starting Lines.
Operation and Repair Stations exist at valid Sites.
At least one valid Shift exists.

sections.title: Define Products and Materials
sections.label: Define Products
sections.description: Organise products, create components and variants, build BOMs, and choose the correct material tracking approach.

pages.title: Projects and Product Families
pages.summary: Use the recommended hierarchy to keep products, reporting, and future growth organised.
steps: Create a Project for a meaningful programme, product programme, or managed manufacturing scope.
Create Product Families inside Projects to group closely related Products.
Assign Products to the appropriate Product Family during Product setup.
Use consistent naming so Work Orders and reports can inherit a useful hierarchy.
rules: A Product Family requires a Project.
Fynd ERP can create a Product without a Product Family, but the hierarchy improves organisation and reporting.
Use Variants for versions of the same Product, not for unrelated Products.
checklist: Projects have a clear purpose.
Product Families group genuinely related Products.
The hierarchy will remain understandable as more Products are added.

pages.title: Create Components
pages.summary: Create the material and part records that will be used in Product BOMs and shop-floor validation.
steps: Create a Component for every material or part that must be planned, scanned, consumed, or traced.
Enter the required name, code, and unit; names and codes require at least two characters.
Choose one mutually exclusive mode: Serialized, Consumable, or Fixed Serial.
For Fixed Serial, enter the permanent barcode or QR value.
Set maximum stock above minimum stock and keep the reorder level between them.
Load or receive inventory before the Component is needed for production.
rules: Unit and tracking settings cannot be changed after creation.
BOMs reference Component records, so Components must exist first.
Serialised Components require a valid individual identifier during consumption.
Quantity-based Components are validated against the required BOM quantity.
checklist: Every BOM material has a Component record.
Tracking type matches the physical identification method.
Units of measure and quantities are consistent.

pages.title: Create Products and Variants
pages.summary: Create finished-product definitions and decide when Variants are useful.
steps: Create the Product with a unique name of at least two characters and SKU of at least three characters.
Assign the recommended Product Family when available.
Add at least two Variants when the same Product has meaningful configurations.
Add a shared BOM or provide BOM entries for every Variant.
Use shared BOM rows for every Variant and Variant rows only to override matching quantities.
Configure a serial number template when a specific finished-unit format is needed.
rules: A Product without Variants requires a shared BOM.
A Product with Variants needs a shared BOM or a BOM for every Variant.
If Variants are used, a Work Order must select the required Variant.
The serial number template is optional, but unit serial generation before release is not.
checklist: Product name and SKU are unique.
Variant use is deliberate and consistent.
Every Product configuration has BOM coverage.

pages.title: Build the Bill of Materials
pages.summary: Define exactly which Components and quantities are required to build the Product.
steps: Review the initial draft BOM created during Product setup.
Confirm every required Component and quantity per finished unit.
Use shared entries for common materials and Variant entries only where requirements differ.
Review units of measure and effective quantities before activation.
Resolve non-positive quantities and duplicate Components within the same scope.
rules: BOM items can be edited only while the Version is Draft.
Routing creation requires an active BOM belonging to the selected Product.
The pre-start readiness check uses the active BOM to calculate material requirements.
Changing an active BOM can change future production readiness and should be controlled.
checklist: The BOM contains every required production Component.
Quantities match one finished unit.
Variant overrides do not duplicate shared requirements incorrectly.

pages.title: Activate a BOM Version
pages.summary: Move the reviewed BOM from draft to the active production version required by Routing.
steps: Open the Product's BOM Version and review its status and items.
Confirm the BOM contains at least one item.
Select Release BOM Version and confirm the edit-lock warning.
Verify the active status, removed editing controls, and enabled Create Routing action.
rules: Only reviewed draft or approved versions should be released.
An empty BOM cannot be released as a meaningful production definition.
Releasing locks the BOM Version, and only one Version is active for the Product at a time.
Routing must use an active BOM from the same Product.
checklist: The correct BOM Version is active.
The active BOM belongs to the intended Product.
Material inventory exists or has a replenishment plan.

pages.title: Serial, Lot, and Mixed Material Tracking
pages.summary: Choose how components are traced while keeping finished production aligned with Fynd ERP's unit-serial model.
steps: Use lot or batch information to trace bulk input material back to its source.
Use serialised Component tracking when each individual part must be bound to a finished unit.
Use quantity consumption for non-serialised Components.
Combine both tracking types in one BOM when the Product uses mixed materials.
rules: Normal Fynd ERP Work Orders still create one finished-unit serial and Production Task per output unit.
A serial number batch groups finished-unit serials; it is not a quantity-only production mode.
Material genealogy is strongest when lots, serials, and consumption events are captured at the correct Station.
checklist: Every Component has the correct tracking type.
Lot identifiers are available for batch-tracked inputs.
The team understands that finished output remains unit-serialised.

sections.title: Design the Production Process
sections.label: Design the Process
sections.description: Turn the product definition into an executable route, connect Stations, assign Lines, and prepare identifiers.

pages.title: Routing in Plain Language
pages.summary: Understand how a Routing tells Fynd ERP where a unit goes and what happens at each operation.
steps: A Routing is created for a Product, one or more Variants, and an active BOM Version.
Each operation node points to a real Station and includes a mandatory Repair Station.
Connect Start, every operation stage, and End to define the execution order.
Conditional branches can use a quality result; lower priority numbers are evaluated first.
rules: Assigned Components and quantities must both reach 100% BOM coverage.
More than one Routing can be Active; the Routing is determined when the Work Order starts.
Components and tools can be attached to the operation where they are needed.
checklist: I can explain the route from Start to End.
Every operation maps to a real Station.
Failure paths have an intentional destination.

pages.title: Create and Validate a Routing
pages.summary: Build a connected production workflow that passes Fynd ERP's Routing validation.
steps: Open the Product detail and select Create Routing.
Select at least one Variant, continue, and select an Active BOM Version.
Enter the required Workflow Name, add an optional description, and set Active as needed.
Select Add Stage and Create Manually; choose the main Station, enter a unique Operation Name, and select a different Repair Station.
Assign the required Components and quantities until both BOM coverage indicators reach 100%.
Save the stage and connect Start to every stage and then End. Save becomes available when the workflow is valid.
Select Save, review the summary, select Confirm & Save, and verify the Routing detail page.
rules: The Product is supplied by the Product detail page; at least one Variant, an active BOM Version, and a Workflow Name are required.
A Routing needs at least one operation Station.
Every operation requires a Repair Station different from its main Station.
Component and quantity coverage must both reach 100% of the selected BOM.
Start, every operation stage, and End must be connected; Save remains unavailable until automatic validation passes.
checklist: The intended Product Variants and Active BOM are selected.
Every operation has valid main and Repair Stations and full BOM coverage.
Start, every stage, and End are connected and the workflow is valid.
The Routing detail page shows the expected status, Product, Variants, BOM, and Workflow Preview.

pages.title: Assign Products to Lines
pages.summary: Tell Fynd ERP which active Lines are allowed to receive tasks for a Product.
steps: Open the Product detail and scroll to Assigned Lines.
Select Assign Line and open the Select Line control.
Review Available Lines separately from Lines assigned to other Products; use the code and Site to choose the correct Line.
Select Assign, then repeat only for other Lines that can physically manufacture the same Product.
Verify each assigned Line's name, code, status, capacity per hour, Site, and actions in the table.
rules: At least one Line assignment is needed to enable multi-line Work Order execution for the Product.
Assign only Lines that can physically manufacture the Product.
Starting-Line eligibility is configured separately on the Line, not in the Product assignment dialog.
checklist: The Product has at least one eligible assigned Line.
Assigned Line codes and Sites match the intended physical process.
The table shows the expected status and capacity for every assignment.

pages.title: Starting Lines and Capacity
pages.summary: Configure where newly released units enter production and how Fynd ERP prevents Line overload.
steps: Open Process & Engineering → Line, search by name or code, open the Line detail, and select Edit.
Optionally set Capacity Per Hour and Capacity Per Shift; when both are supplied, the shift value must be greater than the hourly value.
Optionally set Task Queue Capacity to the maximum pending and active tasks allowed on the Line.
Turn on Is Starting Line only when the Line may receive the initial task during capacity planning.
Select Save and verify the status, Site, capacity values, and assigned Products on the Line detail.
rules: Only Lines marked as Starting Lines can receive the initial task during capacity planning.
The UI identifies the manufacturing phase order as SMT → BLT → ASSEMBLY → TESTING → PACKING.
Capacity Per Shift must be greater than Capacity Per Hour when both optional values are supplied.
Task Queue Capacity is optional; when supplied, it must be a whole number from 1 to 100,000.
checklist: Starting-Line status reflects the real first manufacturing phase.
Hourly, shift, and queue capacity values are valid and realistic.
The Line detail shows the intended Site, status, capacities, and assigned Products.

pages.title: Configure Product Identifiers
pages.summary: Prepare serial, range, template, or bundle identifiers that must be assigned when Production Tasks are created.
steps: Open Process & Engineering → Identifier Management and select Create Identifier Range → Create Manually.
Enter the required Name and choose Range, Template, External, or Manual as the source.
For a Range source, select the identifier Type and Range or File Upload. Enter required Start and End values for a generated range, review its count, and select Create.
Open Production → Products, open the Product detail, scroll to Product Identifiers, and select Add Identifier.
Select the identifier definition, enter the required Identifier Key and Display Name, and choose Generated or External.
Choose On Task Creation, On Task Start, or At Route Step; enable Auto-generate and Must be Unique when required.
Select Add Identifier and verify the Product table shows the expected source, timing, and linked range.
rules: Identifier range Name is required, and a single operation can process no more than 10,000 identifiers.
Generated identifiers are created by the system; External identifiers are scanned or entered by an operator.
Product Identifier Keys are stored in uppercase.
At Route Step timing requires configuration in the Routing Editor.
checklist: The identifier definition is Active and exposes the intended values and availability.
The Product mapping has the correct key, type, source, and assignment timing.
Auto-generation and uniqueness match the identifier's business rule.

sections.title: Plan and Launch Production
sections.label: Plan and Launch
sections.description: Create production demand, generate unit serials, plan Line capacity, validate readiness, and release work safely.

pages.title: Production Order vs Work Order
pages.summary: Choose the right planning record and understand which one creates executable production.
steps: Use a Production Order to group and monitor related Work Orders. Name and a unique Order Number are required; Client is optional and restricts the Work Orders that can be grouped.
Use a Work Order as the executable manufacturing record for a Product with Routing, input quantity, priority, due date, and Shifts.
Use Test Order only for production-line setup or workflow testing because Test Orders are excluded from analytics.
rules: A Production Order groups Work Orders and does not define executable quantity by itself.
A Work Order can exist without being grouped under a Production Order.
At least one Shift is required before a Work Order can be started.
Test Orders are not calculated in production analytics.
checklist: Grouping demand uses a Production Order with the intended client restriction.
Every executable quantity is represented by a routed Work Order.
Test Order is enabled only for non-analytics setup or workflow testing.

pages.title: Create a Work Order
pages.summary: Create an executable production instruction after all Product and factory dependencies are ready.
flow: Enter quantity, priority, and due date
steps: Enter a unique Work Order name.
Select a Product with a configured Routing, then select the required Product Variant; Project and Product Family are derived automatically.
Enter a positive Input Quantity, choose the required Priority, and select a Due Date that is not in the past.
Review Total Computed Quantity, which equals Input Quantity multiplied by the Product Multiplier.
Assign one or more Shifts when known, review Component Availability, and create the Work Order.
rules: Name, routed Product, Product Variant, Input Quantity, Priority, and Due Date are required.
The Due Date cannot be in the past, and computed quantity equals Input Quantity × Product Multiplier.
Shift is optional at creation, but at least one Shift is required before the Work Order can start.
Test Orders are intended for line setup or workflow testing and are excluded from analytics.
A successfully created Work Order begins in PENDING status.
checklist: Product, Variant, quantity, priority, and due date are correct.
The computed quantity and Component Availability panel are reviewed.
A Shift is assigned now or planned before start, and Test Order is off for normal production.

pages.title: Generate and Confirm Unit Serials
pages.summary: Create exactly one finished-unit serial for every unit before releasing a normal Work Order.
steps: Select Start Work Order; the Serial Numbers step blocks progress until confirmed serials equal the Work Order quantity.
Select Generate Serial Numbers and use the Product Template when configured, another available Template, or Manual Upload for CSV or Excel.
Verify the preview count, select Validate Uniqueness, and generate the batch.
Select Confirm & Complete, then verify CONFIRMED and the exact serial count in the start journey.
rules: Confirmed serial count must exactly equal the Work Order quantity before the next start step is enabled.
Product Template is unavailable when no template is configured for the Product.
Every proposed serial must pass uniqueness validation.
A GENERATED batch is not production-ready until Confirm & Complete changes it to CONFIRMED.
A serial number batch groups unit serials; it does not replace unit-level identities.
checklist: The serial batch status is CONFIRMED.
The confirmed serial count equals Work Order quantity.
Serial format is suitable for scanning and traceability.

pages.title: Plan Capacity and Select Routing
pages.summary: Confirm eligible Starting Lines have enough headroom and choose the active Product Routing.
steps: After confirmed serials match quantity, open Capacity & Lines and select Configure Capacity Planning.
Review Total Quantity, Available Capacity, Available Lines, and projected capacity on eligible Starting Lines.
Use system-optimized distribution or manual assignment; in system mode, select Proceed with System Assignment.
Confirm capacity planning completed, then select the eligible active Production Route.
Verify the route option's BOM status, route type, item count, and enabled Next action.
rules: Capacity planning is disabled until serials are confirmed for the full Work Order quantity.
Available queue capacity on eligible Starting Lines must cover the Work Order quantity.
The selected Production Route must be eligible and show an active associated BOM.
checklist: Capacity planning is complete.
No Line exceeds its queue capacity.
The correct active Routing is selected.

pages.title: Pre-Start Validation and Release
pages.summary: Use Fynd ERP's readiness checks to fix blockers before Production Tasks are created.
steps: After Serial Numbers, Capacity & Lines, and Routing are complete, select Run Pre-Start Validation.
Review Product assignment, BOM, generated and confirmed serials, Component Inventory, Station-Level Inventory, and Identifier Availability.
Resolve first-stage Station shortages with Transfer All or a component transfer; use Auto-Fill Shortage for the exact remaining quantity.
Refresh until validation shows PASS, then select Proceed to Start.
rules: A first-stage Station shortage blocks start even when plant-level Component Inventory is sufficient.
Transfer All prioritizes storage locations, then non-routing Stations, and may perform partial transfers.
Proceed to Start releases immediately, creates Production Tasks, and changes the Work Order to IN PROGRESS.
Validation must show PASS before Proceed to Start is enabled.
checklist: All blockers are resolved.
Warnings have an understood mitigation.
The Work Order changes to In Progress and creates the expected number of Production Tasks.

sections.title: Run Production
sections.label: Run the Shop Floor
sections.description: Understand Production Tasks, operator execution, material consumption, and the status trail created during work.

pages.title: Production Tasks
pages.summary: Understand the unit-level record operators execute after a Work Order is released.
steps: Open Production Tasks on the released Work Order and verify one Task exists for each confirmed serial.
Review task distribution by Line Type and Line, then open a unit Task.
Confirm Task status, assigned serial, Work Order, Product, Line, and Line Type.
Review Stage Progress, Bound Identifiers, BOM Progress, and Routing and Process Details.
rules: Release creates one Production Task per confirmed finished-unit serial.
Capacity planning provides the initial Line assignment, and the selected Routing defines the current Stage and Station.
Required BOM components remain Pending until consumed during execution.
Generated Product identifiers can be bound to the Task before execution begins.
checklist: Task count matches Work Order quantity.
Every Task has a serial and eligible Line.
Operators can find Tasks at the correct Station.

pages.title: Operator Execution Flow
pages.summary: Follow the normal sequence an operator uses to process a unit at a Station.
steps: In Operator, select the Product first, choose Mapped, and use the Status filter if the Station is hidden by the default Running view.
Open the Station, select an active Work Order, and choose an eligible Production Line.
Scan or enter the Production Task ID or confirmed finished-unit serial, then select Start Task.
Enter an available serial for every serialised BOM Component and satisfy each configured identifier validator.
Confirm the result and select Complete & Next so Fynd ERP records execution and Route progress.
rules: Mapped Stations are product-aware; select the Product before using the Mapped filter.
Only active Work Orders and eligible Production Lines are offered for the selected Station.
Required Component identities must be available and valid; the Battery Pack validator requires GS1 AI 01 and AI 10.
Complete & Next records the operator, Station, material identities, result, timestamps, and Route progress.
checklist: The Product, Station, Work Order, Line, Task, and Routing step match.
Every required Component identity validates successfully.
The completion is visible in Task History and Route history.

pages.title: Material Consumption During Production
pages.summary: Capture the material used by each unit so inventory and genealogy remain accurate.
prerequisites: Serial, Lot, and Mixed Material Tracking
steps: Transfer required stock to the execution Station and confirm the Station inventory covers the BOM requirement.
Scan or enter the Production Task ID or confirmed finished-unit serial in the Station work area.
Enter one available, unconsumed serial for every serialised BOM Component and satisfy its configured identifier validator.
Select Complete & Next after all required inputs validate.
Verify the Production Task is COMPLETED and the material identities appear in consumption and genealogy history.
rules: Serialised Components require a unique available serial; an already consumed serial is rejected.
Configured identifier validators apply during execution; the Battery Pack requires GS1 AI 01 and AI 10.
Material should be transferred before the unit reaches the Station that consumes it.
Completion records material identities, inventory use, and genealogy against the Production Task.
checklist: Station inventory covers current production.
Every serialised Component identity is unique, available, and valid.
The completed Task and consumed identities are visible in production and traceability history.

pages.title: Statuses and Route Logs
pages.summary: Read the history Fynd ERP creates as Work Orders and units move through production.
steps: Open the Work Order to review overall status, progress, Production Metrics, and task distribution.
Open Route Execution Logs and compare Total Logs, Passed, Failed, and In Progress.
Filter by status, date range, Work Order, Product, Routing, or Station.
Review the timestamp, production context, operator, quality result, and execution status in each log.
rules: Work Order status and Task status answer different questions.
A Work Order becomes COMPLETED only after every Production Task finishes.
Route Execution Logs preserve operation-level evidence, including the Station, operator, quality result, status, and timestamp.
checklist: Work Order progress and task distribution agree.
Completed operations appear in Route Execution Logs.
Filters return the expected Work Order, Product, Routing, or Station history.

sections.title: Quality and Exceptions
sections.label: Manage Quality
sections.description: Configure inspections and handle failures through defects, NCR, repair, rework, hold, scrap, and teardown.

pages.title: Configure Quality Controls
pages.summary: Decide where inspection, sampling, and verification belong in the manufacturing route.
steps: Open Quality → Control Points and select Create Control Point.
Enter the unique Code and Name, then select Control Type, Frequency, and On Failure.
Select the Production Line first, then choose the Station that becomes available.
Choose the failure action, enable Auto-hold failed units when required, and add checklist questions.
Create the control and verify its Active status, scope, failure action, and checklist on Configuration.
rules: Code, Name, Control Type, Frequency, and On Failure are required.
Station remains unavailable until a Production Line is selected.
Failure action can Stop Line, Quarantine, Hold Lot, Escalate, or Alert Only.
Checklist questions define the evidence operators must record.
checklist: The Control Point is Active and has a unique Code.
Line and Station scope are correct.
Failure action, Auto-hold behavior, and checklist questions match the production risk.

pages.title: Inspections, Defects, NCR, and CAPA
pages.summary: Run a configured inspection, record failed samples, and understand the current NCR and CAPA limitations in SIT.
steps: Create and activate the applicable inspection configuration before starting an inspection.
Choose either a Work Order or an available, non-expired Lot—never both—and enter the required total and sample quantities.
Record each sample and its checks. A failed sample requires a Defect code and Severity before it can be saved.
Reject the inspection and choose whether to hold only failed serials or the entire lot. Inspection-local defects and plant Defects are separate records.
Treat NCR and CAPA as unavailable from these screens in the current SIT build: Create NCR opens ‘NCR report not found’, and CAPA Management has no create action.
rules: An active inspection configuration is a prerequisite; Plant scope is the fallback and more specific scopes override it.
A source is either a Work Order or a Lot, and total quantity is required.
A failed sample cannot be saved without Defect details.
checklist: The inspection configuration is Active.
The source, quantities, sample serial, checks, and Defect details are complete.
The selected hold scope matches the rejected output.

pages.title: Repair and Rework
pages.summary: Configure repair intake, record rework evidence, and understand the current SIT completion limitation.
steps: In Repair Config, enable Auto-create repair on failure and select a Default Repair Station when automatic intake is required.
Use Debug Queue to triage incoming failures. Rework Board jobs originate from a failure or Disposition; the board has no create action.
Review the linked Work Order, serial, mechanism, attempt number, and current board column.
Select Record work and enter labor minutes, material cost, and concise work notes before selecting Complete Work.
In the current SIT build, Complete Work saves labor and cost but leaves the job In Progress; notes clear on reopen and re-inspection does not start.
rules: Auto-create repair and the Default Repair Station control automatic queue intake.
Attempt Limit rules are configured under Alerts and can alert, block, or block and propose scrap.
Total and per-line repair WIP caps are optional; leaving a cap empty disables that limit.
checklist: The job remains linked to the original serial and Work Order.
Labor minutes, material cost, and work notes are entered.
The current SIT completion limitation is understood before relying on re-inspection.

pages.title: Hold, Scrap, and Teardown
pages.summary: Create scoped holds, track controlled scrap dispatches, and start teardown only from eligible executed scrap.
steps: Open Quality → Hold Management → Create Hold and choose the Hold Level before selecting a target.
Select the required target and Reason. Notes are optional, and a Work Order hold can include an optional expected release date.
Submit inventory lot, vendor, and date-code holds for approval; they remain inactive until Quality approves them.
Configure Scrap Reasons first, then use Scrap Register to track Pending Approval, Approved, Executed, and Rejected dispatches. The register has no create action.
Use Send to teardown on an executed Scrap dispatch to create a Teardown order linked to the donor serial and recovered Components.
rules: Hold Level determines the target and impact; a Work Order hold pauses all production for that order.
Inventory lot, vendor, and date-code holds require Quality approval.
Teardown cannot begin until Scrap is executed and explicitly sent to teardown.
checklist: The target and Reason are selected for the correct Hold Level.
Scrap reason categories and reason codes exist before dispatch.
The teardown order remains linked to its donor serial and Scrap dispatch.

sections.title: Package, Ship, and Trace
sections.label: Package and Trace
sections.description: Configure container operations, verify shipment readiness, and trace finished units and materials across their lifecycle.

pages.title: Packaging in Fynd ERP
pages.summary: Understand how unit, container, label, weight, and closure operations fit into a Routing.
steps: Open Packaging & Shipping and select Packaging.
Open Packing Configuration, select the Product, and define its product-specific container type. Product, Name, and Code are required; Code accepts 2–10 alphanumeric characters.
Leave Child Container Type empty for a leaf that binds finished-unit serials directly, or select a child to build the Device → Box → Carton → Pallet hierarchy.
Return to the Packaging Dashboard, select Create Container, and choose the Product, required Container Type, and required Work Order ID.
Open the generated UID to review device count, weight and dimensions, linked Work Order, label state, and History.
rules: Packing configurations are product-specific.
A leaf has no child container type and binds serial numbers directly; parent configurations accept the selected child type.
Create Container remains disabled until Container Type and Work Order ID are selected.
A UID template is optional; when omitted, Fynd ERP uses the default UID format.
Pallets are added to Shipments, which are managed separately in the Shipments module.
checklist: Product-specific container configuration is active.
Device → Box → Carton → Pallet hierarchy matches the physical flow.
Container is linked to the correct Work Order.
UID, device count, label state, and History are visible before closure.

pages.title: Containers and Labels
pages.summary: Create a clear packaging identity from individual units through cartons and pallets.
steps: In Packing Configuration, create the leaf first, then create each parent with its allowed Child Container Type; selecting a child makes Max child count required.
Choose a container-specific UID Template and sequence reset scope, then configure dimensions, weight range, and tolerance.
Create the parent from the Packaging Dashboard by selecting the Product, parent Container Type, and completed Work Order.
In Pack by UID, scan a finished serial, device UID, child UID, identifier, or task ID; a valid unit automatically creates the configured leaf and packs it into the parent.
Print the carton label and verify carton UID, model, quantity, unit serial, QR codes, History, and the Reprint path.
rules: Use a container-specific UID pattern so generated container identities do not collide with unit serials.
A parent accepts only its configured child type, and its maximum child count is enforced.
Only eligible production identities can be packed; source values unavailable to the label remain blank.
checklist: Leaf and parent types mirror the physical hierarchy.
UID template, capacity, dimensions, weight, and tolerance are correct.
Packing, printed label content, History, and Reprint have been checked.

pages.title: Shipment Verification
pages.summary: Verify that packaged output matches shipment requirements before dispatch.
steps: Open Shipment Verification and select an existing Shipment; Container Type, counts, container rows, and Export remain unavailable until the required Shipment is selected.
Confirm an active Shipment Rule includes the selected container configuration and permits its container-count and maximum-weight limits.
Confirm the Shipping Gate has positive remaining approved Purchase Order quantity; the current active SIT gate is fully consumed with balance 0.
Use a client- or product-scoped ASN template for the Excel export; this SIT Plant currently has no ASN templates.
Current SIT limitation: the Plant has no Shipments, and Create Shipment omits backend-required lines and warehouseRootLocationId, so verification cannot begin from this UI.
rules: Shipment selection is mandatory before Container Type or verification data becomes available.
The governing Shipment Rule and a positive Shipping Gate balance are prerequisites.
ASN output is client- or product-scoped when a template is configured.
checklist: A valid Shipment exists and can be selected.
The active rule covers the container configuration, count, and weight.
Shipping Gate balance is positive and the required ASN template exists.

pages.title: Traceability, Genealogy, and Recall
pages.summary: Follow a finished unit back to its Work Order, operations, Components, material lots, containers, and shipment.
steps: In Master Traceability, combine filters and unlock dependent Product filters from their parent selection. A specific identifier list overrides the other filters, and Generate Dossier remains disabled until at least one scope is selected.
Select only the required dossier sheets. Generation is asynchronous and completed files remain in Recent exports; the Nova X1 Work Order produced a two-unit dossier.
For Stage Timeline, select a date range, at least one Work Order, and 1–50 Operations. The date range is required even though this SIT build does not mark it with an asterisk.

Use the full genealogy tree with a pallet, carton, box, device, product, Component, or batch identifier. Downstream follows a finished identity to Components and lots; Upstream follows a lot toward finished units.
Use Find Affected Units with a Batch/Lot Number or Component Serial. The Nova X1 battery lot returned NOVA-X1-PHONE-000002 as an affected finished serial.

Recall creation requires Title and Severity. In this SIT build, By Batch finds no production tasks and direct completed-task assignment fails because productionTaskIds is unused, so the authorized Nova X1 Recall Notice remains Draft with zero affected units.
rules: Traceability quality depends on accurate scanning and consumption during production.
A specific identifier list overrides the other dossier scope filters.
Stage Timeline requires a date range, at least one Work Order, and 1–50 Operations.
A recall notice controls the response; traceability identifies the affected scope, but affected-unit assignment is currently blocked in SIT.
checklist: The completed two-unit Nova X1 dossier appears in Recent exports.
The Nova X1 serial resolves to its consumed display and battery lots.
The battery lot returns NOVA-X1-PHONE-000002 as affected.
The authorized Recall Notice remains Draft with zero affected units until the SIT assignment defect is fixed.

sections.title: Operate and Improve
sections.label: Operate and Improve
sections.description: Use dashboards, shift handovers, maintenance, tools, reports, and audit history to keep production controlled.

pages.title: Dashboards and Production Monitoring
pages.summary: Choose the dashboard that answers the operational question instead of treating every metric as the same.
steps: Use the Dashboard to review setup readiness, active Work Orders, production Stations, active Products, Clients, Projects, production completion, and quality targets for the selected Plant.

In Work Orders, evaluate Status, Priority, and Due Date together. Past-due active records are marked Delayed; the Nova X1 list separates the completed original Work Order from its in-progress repair Work Order.

Open the completed Nova X1 Work Order to review 2/2 tasks, 2.9 units/hour, 20m 56s takt and cycle time, 100% yield, and 42m total execution time. Yield is passed quality steps divided by completed steps, with a displayed target of at least 95%.
Use Track Progress for the live board. It auto-refreshes every 30 seconds by default and supports Station filters, completed highlighting, samples-only, sorting, and fullscreen.

Use Production Tasks to verify Serial, task ID, grouping, Work Order, Line, Product/Routing, and status. A serial can have multiple task records, including a later repair task, so confirm the Work Order and Line before acting.
Use Route Logs to verify the Work Order, Product, Routing, Line, Station, operator, timestamp, quality status, and execution status. The two Nova X1 logs are Passed and Complete.
rules: A dashboard summarises records; the underlying records remain the source of evidence.
Route Log summary totals reflect the current filters.
Takt and cycle metrics use completed execution time; yield is passed quality steps divided by completed steps.
The same serial can have multiple task records, so task status must be interpreted with its Work Order and Line.
checklist: Plant-level counts and targets match the selected Plant.
The completed and repair Nova X1 Work Orders are distinguished correctly.
The live board shows two completed Nova X1 tasks and two logs.
Both Nova X1 Route Logs show Passed and Complete with operator and Station evidence.

pages.title: Shift Operations and Handovers
pages.summary: Maintain continuity when production responsibility moves from one Shift to another.
steps: Confirm net working time after unpaid breaks. Nova X1 Assembly Morning Shift runs 06:00–14:00; its 15-minute unpaid tea break reduces 8 hours to 7h 45m net.

Verify Shift Schedule coverage. New Schedules remain Draft until activated, but status alone does not prove coverage: all three current SIT Schedules show 0 shifts/week, including the Active Standard and Weekend Schedules.
Create a Shift Handover. Shift and Handover Date are required; Line, outgoing/incoming operators, summaries, notes, pending tasks, and checklist items are optional.
Connect the authorized Nova X1 Handover to NOVA-X1-SHIFT-A and NOVA_X1_LINE_01, then record completed production, passed Route Logs, equipment state, safety, and two pending repair tasks.

Review the Draft before completion. Outgoing Supervisor defaults to the current Plant Administrator, Incoming Supervisor may remain blank, and Complete should be used only after the next Shift reviews the record.
Use Break Compliance carefully: with zero Break Logs, SIT displays 100% compliance and 0 violations, while Export CSV remains disabled until filtered records exist.
rules: Unpaid breaks are deducted from Shift duration when net working time is calculated.
A Schedule marked Active can still have zero assigned shifts and no effective coverage.
A new Handover is Draft; Complete it only after the receiving Shift reviews the recorded context.
A 100% Break Compliance rate with zero Break Logs does not prove compliant breaks occurred.
checklist: Nova X1 Shift net working time is 7h 45m after its unpaid break.
The authorized Handover is connected to the Nova X1 Shift and Final Assembly Line.
Production, quality, equipment, safety, and pending repair work are recorded.
The Draft is reviewed before Complete is selected.

pages.title: Tools, Equipment, and Maintenance
pages.summary: Keep required production assets available, correctly located, and safe to use.
steps: Open the child Tools and Equipments page and supply the required Tool Name, Tool Code, Tool Category, Manufacturer, Model, Station, and Status.
Enable Requires Calibration only when the Tool is governed; this reveals interval and provider fields.
Record Calibration Date, Next Calibration Date, and Result so a governed Tool moves from Unknown to a current calibration state.
Use Trigger Maintenance Check to evaluate configured rules; no matching rules returns 0 alerts and leaves Export disabled when there are no rows.
Create a Maintenance Work Order with the required Tool and Title, then move it through Draft, Submitted, and Approved before Start is available.
rules: Tool Name, Tool Code, Tool Category, Manufacturer, Model, Station, and Status are required.
A calibration-governed Tool remains Unknown until a calibration record defines its result and next due date; overrides remain auditable.
Maintenance Work Orders require Tool and Title, default to Medium and Corrective, and cannot be started before approval.
checklist: The Tool is assigned to the intended Nova X1 Station and has the correct status.
Calibration evidence, certificate, and next due date are current when required.
The approved maintenance window is scheduled and the order has not been started early.

pages.title: Reports, Exports, and Audit Trail
pages.summary: Use reports and immutable history to explain production results and configuration changes.
flow: Create a filtered Work Order export
steps: In Master Traceability, combine optional scope filters or use a pasted/uploaded serial-number list, which overrides the other scope filters.
Select the required dossier sheets, generate the report, and wait for Recent exports to show Completed, the unit count, and the XLSX filename.
From Work Orders, open Export Work Orders and re-apply Search, Status, and Priority in the separate Create Data Export dialog because list filters are not inherited.
Open Export Details to confirm type, format, state, file size, applied filters, processed rows, and progress before downloading.
Use View all changes for actor, action, affected Work Order, and timestamp; the current View All History destination returns an error in SIT.
rules: A serial-number list overrides the other Master Traceability scope filters.
A Completed export is not sufficient evidence by itself; verify processed rows, progress, file size, applied filters, and file contents.
Recent Changes is currently usable, while View All History is unavailable in SIT.
checklist: The dossier scope and selected sheets match the investigation question.
The operational export contains the intended filtered records.
Recent Changes identifies who changed the Nova X1 Work Order and when.

sections.title: Help and Reference
sections.label: Help and Reference
sections.description: Use checklists, requirement matrices, terminology, and decision trees when setting up or troubleshooting Fynd ERP.

pages.title: Required, Recommended, and Conditional Setup
pages.summary: Use one matrix to understand which records block production and which improve control.
steps: Required: Site for Stations; Lines; operation and Repair Stations; Shifts; Components; Product and BOM; active BOM; Routing; Product-to-Line assignment; confirmed unit serials.
Recommended: Projects, Product Families, explicit capacity, Site assignment on Lines, dashboards, handovers, reporting, and trial production.
Conditional: Product Variants, additional identifiers, tools, automations, quality sampling, packaging, shipment, repair, rework, and recall configuration.
rules: Required labels reflect the supported normal production journey.
Recommended records may not be database blockers but prevent avoidable operational confusion.
Conditional features become required when the selected production design depends on them.
checklist: Required setup is complete.
Recommended structure has been reviewed.
Every conditional capability has an explicit use or exclusion decision.

pages.title: First Production Run Checklist
pages.summary: Run a small controlled Work Order to validate the complete configuration before scaling volume.
steps: Use a small quantity that is large enough to test serials, capacity, and material consumption.
Run at least one unit through the complete normal route.
Test a controlled failure and Repair path.
Verify quality, packaging, and shipment steps that apply.
Trace a completed unit back to material and forward to its container or shipment.
rules: Do not use the first full-volume order as the first complete process test.
Record every configuration issue and retest after correction.
The trial is complete only when the unit history is understandable end to end.
checklist: Work Order creates the expected Production Tasks.
Normal and failure paths work.
Material consumption and inventory are correct.
Packaging and shipment work where configured.
End-to-end traceability is complete.

pages.title: Troubleshooting Decision Tree
pages.summary: Start with the failing action and work backward through its dependencies.
steps: If Product creation fails, check BOM coverage and Variant rules.
If Routing creation fails, check active BOM, Stations, Repair Stations, and connectivity.
If Work Order creation fails, check Routing, active Line assignment, Shift, Product, and Variant.
If release fails, check serial count, Starting Line, capacity, active BOM, inventory, and required identifiers.
If an operation cannot complete, check current route, Station, required inputs, quality gates, and exception status.
rules: Keep the exact error message; do not troubleshoot from memory.
Confirm the record belongs to the current Plant.
Fix the earliest missing dependency instead of changing downstream data.
checklist: The blocked action is clearly identified.
The immediate prerequisite has been checked.
The correction is verified with the smallest safe retry.

pages.title: Fynd ERP Glossary
pages.summary: Use globally neutral definitions for the core records and actions in Fynd ERP.
steps: Plant: the manufacturing context that owns and isolates operational data.
Site: a physical location within the Plant.
Line: a production lane that receives unit-level tasks.
Station: a work point used by a Routing operation.
BOM: the Components and quantities required for a Product.
Routing: the connected sequence of operations a unit follows.
Work Order: the executable instruction to produce a Product quantity.
Production Task: one finished unit moving through production.
Genealogy: the relationship between finished units, consumed material, packaging, and shipment.
rules: Use Product for finished output and Component for input material.
Use Production Order for grouping and Work Order for execution.
Use Repair for fixing a failed unit and Rework for repeating controlled manufacturing operations.
checklist: Terminology is used consistently in procedures and training.
Local factory terms are mapped to the Fynd ERP term.
Users can distinguish similarly named records.

pages.title: Capability Availability Guide
pages.summary: Recognise which capabilities are always part of the core flow and which appear only when configured.
steps: Core flow includes factory records, Products, BOMs, Routings, Lines, Shifts, Work Orders, serials, Production Tasks, and history.
Quality, repair, packaging, identifiers, tools, automations, and shipment depend on configuration.
Some capabilities can be Product-specific, Variant-specific, Routing-specific, Station-specific, or Plant-specific.
Confirm availability in the current Fynd ERP environment before writing local procedures.
rules: Do not assume every menu item is required for every manufacturing process.
Do not describe proposed or unverified capabilities as available.
Use the latest verified implementation and active configuration as the source of truth.
checklist: Core and conditional capabilities are clearly separated.
Configured features have been tested in the current environment.
Local training includes only available capabilities.
